text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — need a refreshed battlecard for the Q2 product push. Goal: a 1-page sales sheet + a short routing playbook for inbound. Focus areas: positioning vs cloud AI platforms, LLM API providers, and infra vendors. Deadline: EOD Thurs. @Grant can you own and pull leads from Sales Ops?

Grant: On it. Quick ask — can we standardize to a 30s elevator + 3 win themes and 2 objection responses per competitor? :+1:

Alyssa: I can pull the latest benchmark numbers. Proposal: normalize metrics to 99th-pct latency, $/1M tokens, and a short note on failover behavior. Will post a draft by tomorrow morning. :mag:

Samir: For infra vendors we should highlight: unified runtime (no stitching), predictable unit economics, and private deployment options for regulated customers. I have a 2-line boil down we can use.

Jordan: Webinar tie-in idea — "Operationalizing LLMs: Latency, Cost, and Rollouts". Schedule mid-next-week. Slides needed: 1) benchmark snapshot 2) migration path 3) customer mini-case + CTA to a battlecard download. Ops should get a routing play as part of the CTA.

Grant: Inbound routing (draft):
- MQL arrives -> auto-scan for keywords: "on-prem", "SLA", "latency", "cost"
- If on-prem or compliance -> tag as "Private" -> AE + Solutions Eng handoff (high-touch)
- If low-latency + high-QPS -> tag as "Dedicated interest" -> prioritize for pilot credits
- Cost-sensitive or exploratory -> send Redwood Optimize calc + self-serve guide (SDR nurture)

Alyssa: Benchmark draft (paste):
```
Benchmark snapshot (internal):
- Cloud AI platforms: fastest time-to-value, lower dev work, higher marginal token cost, variable tail latency under burst.
- LLM API providers: simplest integration, limited control for rollouts, often no private option.
- Infra vendors (self-hosted): max control, heavy ops lift, inconsistent developer experience across teams.
Suggested headline: "Predictable inference economics and production SLAs without building infra yourself."```

Samir: Love the headline. For buyer objection "we already use cloud X": response -> "Cloud X is great for prototypes; Redwood gets you predictable unit economics at scale and a clear migration path (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with the same API and tooling."

Maya: Great. Grant — assemble the 1-pager + two objection scripts. Alyssa — finalize numbers and attach a 1-slide benchmark. Jordan — lock webinar date and draft the CTA that triggers the routing playbook. Samir — give me the 2-line infra vendor copy.

Grant: I'll tag Sales Ops and create the handoff doc. Posting a skeleton file in #marketing-assets in a bit.

ops-bot: Reminder — marketing-deck-deadline set for 2026-04-23 17:00 UTC.

Alyssa: Done — uploaded a CSV with normalized metrics and short source notes: internal-benchmarks.csv. Link: https://redwood.internal/bench/2026-q2 (internal only).

Jordan: Booked webinar for 2026-04-28 11:00 PT. Draft CTA: "Download the Redwood Battlecard: Which inference path fits your scale?" Will route registrants into the handoff described above.

Maya: OK looks good. Final ask: keep the public battlecard simple (one page) and put the deeper routing playbook behind gated content for inbound follow-up. Thanks team — please update the skeleton by EOD Thurs. :rocket:
